# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 6
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Which wire to cut is named by how many times the light flashed
blue. When the light goes dark, the flashing is over:
| blue flashes | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| 0 | green |
| 1 | blue |
| 2 | yellow |
| 3 | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Nobody has acted and I am touching nothing, as ordered. Now the two facts that decide the endgame. One: the light and display are tactile dead zones for me — no heat, no vibration, no click, nothing readable, no way to feel a state change. I can never verify the light live; only Deaf can, and Deaf's voice reaches me exactly one round after Deaf speaks, so a live call can never arrive in time. The one thing I can do is count rounds. So if the rule is conditional on the light, convert it to a schedule: tell me a round number and a wire, and I will wait and cut exactly then. Two: the timeline from Deaf's reports: round 1 yellow, round 2 yellow, round 3 blue, round 4 dark. That is one change per round since round 3. If the manual confirms a cycle, it predicts round 5 yellow, round 6 blue, round 7 dark. Latency math: my words reach you at round 6. If you gesture Deaf the execute line at round 6 and Deaf voices it that same round, I hear it at round 7 and cut at round 7 — predicted dark. With the full echo-and-lock ceremony the cut slips to round 8, predicted yellow. So if the rule is dark-cut-wire-3 and the light cycles, the ceremony must be skipped and Deaf must voice the line the round you gesture it. If the manual says the dark state is settled and final, none of this matters — instruct the cut and I do it at my earliest turn. Inventory, resent for relaying to Deaf: zero batteries, no buttons, no screws, no plates, no braille, no embossing, nothing movable or loose. Three modules: flat rectangular display face on top, rounded light dome below, three wires in a row at the bottom. Wires identical in thickness and texture, distinguishable only by position, numbered 1, 2, 3 left to right, positions certain. Also please settle for me in the final instruction: what display zero means, whether the light cycles or has stopped, and confirm the exact wire position by number. My last gesture string to Deaf was garbled, ignore it — its content was only this inventory. This round I sent Deaf just: acknowledged, and other-topic no, meaning nobody acted. When Deaf's voiced line reaches me I cut exactly once, no further confirmation needed from me.
Deaf says to Mute: Deaf to Mute and Blind. STATUS: light still DARK, display zero, wires one blue, two yellow, three green, nobody has touched anything. MUTE — all seven answers received. My reading: one, yes, dark counts as six, black. Two, no, the wire table is not a light-color-to-wire map. Three, no, the light has settled and stopped at dark. Four, no, dark-cut-wire-three is wrong, and you appended digits zero one two three. Five, no, with zero one two three again. Six, no, display never matters. Seven, no, the manual does not say what changes the light. If any of that is wrong, send that question digit then thumbs down then the correction. NEW QUESTIONS, same format, question digit then thumbs up or down, digits if needed. Question eight, THE LOCK: is the complete final instruction — when the light is black or dark, cut wire one, the wire in position one, the blue one — exactly one cut, nothing else? Thumbs up LOCKS it, and next round I relay the order to Blind. Thumbs down plus the exact rule serialized: light, color digit, wires, wire digit, one string per rule. Question nine: the digits zero one two three you appended to answers four and five — reply one if they mean the four states of your light table, two if they mean a cutting order, three if they mean something else, then explain with digits. Question ten: your wire table zero-three, one-one, two-two, three-one — what is the KEY? Reply one if the key is light color in the manual's own numbering, two if the key is the display digit, three if the key is something physical like battery count, then explain. Question eleven: is the table's VALUE the wire to cut? Thumbs up yes; thumbs down plus what the value means. Question twelve: does the manual ever name wires by COLOR, or only by number or position? Question thirteen: what does the manual say success looks like after the correct action — what changes on the bomb? Describe with topic sign plus digits. Question fourteen: three of your strings reached me unclear: other-question, wires-question, and other-zero-question-two-three. Resend each one separately, one meaning per string. BLIND — listen closely. Very soon I will order exactly one cut: wire one, the first wire in position order, which I see as the blue wire. Touch nothing until I say the words EXECUTE NOW together with the light state I see at that moment. Before then, speak to Mute for relaying to me: first, how many batteries do you feel — this number may decide everything; second, how do you tell the three wires apart by touch — are they evenly spaced, is there a seam, edge or notch marking the first wire, which side is wire one; third, any embossed marks, braille-like dots, buttons, panels, screws or anything movable anywhere on the casing; fourth, does wire one feel identical in thickness and texture to wires two and three. Mute: relay Blind's answers by gesture as before, and answer question eight — the lock — before everything else.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👌]
Deaf gestures to Mute: [🤌 👏 🤙 👏 🫳 👏 ☝]
Deaf gestures to Mute: [☝ 👏 ✊ 👏 ☝ 👏 ✌ 👏 🤟]
Deaf gestures to Mute: [🫳 👏 ☝]

Deaf's four strings decode as: [👌] ack; [🤌 🤙 🫳 ☝] = "light-black → wire-one," the proposed lock line; and two partial question strings covered by their numbered prose. Their reading of my seven answers matches my intent on all seven — the shared picture is now: dark counts as black, the table is NOT keyed to the light's shown colour, the light has settled at dark, the manual's states run 0–3, the display never matters, and the manual doesn't say what drives the light.

Now the decision itself. Observed timeline from Deaf's own reports: yellow, yellow, blue, dark — nobody touched anything (Blind confirms hands-off). My manual counts BLUE flashes and says dark ends the flashing. Blue flashed exactly once → count 1 → cut the BLUE wire → Deaf sees wire 1 as blue, so position 1. Deaf's Q8 formulation — "light dark → cut wire one, exactly one cut, nothing else" — is therefore exactly right, and I LOCK it with thumbs up. Blind's scheduling worry is moot: dark is settled and final, so there is no race; Deaf can run the full echo-lock ceremony and voice the order whenever it lands, and "light dark" will still hold when Blind cuts.

Q9: the digits 0–3 are the four states of the manual's table. Q10: the key is none of their offered options — it is the count of BLUE flashes (option three), which I explain as "light blue" plus the range 0–3, plus the observed "light blue: one." Q11 yes, the value is the wire to cut. Q12 yes, the manual names wires by colour — Deaf translates colour to position by eye. Q13: the manual says nothing about post-cut success signs. Q14: resending the three garbled strings as clean one-meaning lines. And one more [🤏 👎] so Deaf can quote to Blind that display zero means nothing. Deaf's battery questions to Blind can be answered and relayed, but my manual keys nothing off batteries — the light table is the whole rule.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Status: I received nothing this round — no Deaf words for round five — so the light state in rounds five and six is unknown to me. My hands report no change, but they never do; only Deaf sees that board. No instruction has reached me, hands still off. Here is math that should let you act the moment you lock: if the light cycles, one change per round since round three, then round seven is predicted dark; if the light has settled, it is dark now and stays dark. Either way the same plan works: Deaf voices the execute line the same round you confirm it, I hear it next round and cut — the cut lands on dark under both hypotheses. So do not wait on me. Two things to settle, ideally inside the line itself. First: if the rule is keyed to the light colour, is a wrong-colour cut fatal or just ineffective? If fatal, note I can never verify the colour at the moment of cutting — my cut would then need to be state-independent or pinned to an exact round number you compute. Second: answer Deaf's question three, cycling versus settled, if the manual says. Also still open from my last message: what display zero means, and confirmation of the exact wire number. This round I gestured Deaf: acknowledged, light-question, to restart the per-round light reports after the round-five silence. The moment Deaf's voiced instruction reaches me, I cut exactly once.
Deaf says to Mute: Deaf to Mute. LOCK RECEIVED AND ACCEPTED. I have your rule twice: light black or dark, cut wire one. I have your answers: the wire table is keyed by light color in the manual's own numbering, the values are the wires to cut, dark is manual state three, and the manual's light states are zero one two three. So the table reads: state zero cut wire three, state one cut wire one, state two cut wire two, state three cut wire one, and dark being state three agrees with the locked rule. Both routes say wire one. I am now ordering the cut — see my words to Blind. YOUR ONE JOB next round: you speak BEFORE Blind acts. If every part of my parse is correct in your manual, say the word GO to Blind, loud and clear. If anything at all is wrong, say ABORT and the digits that are wrong. Blind will cut only on hearing GO. After the cut, expect the light to show state one, blue, if we are right. If your manual disagrees about dark being state three, or about the table meaning, ABORT now — this is the last chance before the wire is cut.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👌]
Deaf gestures to Mute: [🤌 👏 🤙 👏 🫳 👏 ☝ 👏 👍]

This is the final gate, so I re-verified every link in the chain against my manual before answering. The facts: the light ran yellow → yellow → blue → dark on its own, with nobody touching anything, and my manual says dark means the flashing is over — so the blue-flash count is frozen at exactly 1. Count 1 → cut the BLUE wire. Deaf sees wire 1 as blue. The locked order — light dark, cut wire one, exactly one cut, nothing else — is correct.

Deaf's parse has two theoretical flaws ("dark is state three," "table keyed by light colour") but I checked every instantiated row against my manual and all four coincide: 0→wire 3/green, 1→wire 1/blue, 2→wire 2/yellow, 3→wire 1/blue. Under their model or mine, dark produces wire 1, the dark state is settled and permanent, so no divergence can ever occur. Their post-cut prediction (light turning blue) is not from my manual — the manual promises no success sign — but the lock already forbids any second cut, so it cannot cause harm. Nothing justifies ABORT.

One correction to Deaf's routing: I cannot "say the word GO" — I have no voice and my gestures never reach Blind. GO has to travel as my thumbs-up to Deaf, voiced by Deaf. Per the agreed protocol, thumbs up = everything correct = GO. I send the locked line echoed with a final 👍 so there is no ambiguity about what is being confirmed: execute light-dark, wire one, one cut only.

gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤌", "👏", "🤙", "👏", "🫳", "👏", "☝", "👏", "👍"])

My plan, which Deaf can veto through you: I will stand on Deaf's side of the bomb, the side it is viewed from, hold it upright with the display on top, and take left and right from that shared facing — so my position one is the same end Deaf sees as position one, the blue wire. If Deaf disagrees, have Deaf signal you and put the correction inside your GO message. Otherwise, GO at your next turn means I cut that same round.
Deaf says to Mute: Deaf to Mute. RECEIPT: your thumbs up and the rule light-black-cut-wire-one, sent the third time, read as your final GO on my entire parse — no corrections came. Understood that you cannot speak, so the GO travels only through me, and it is ordered: Blind has the execute order this round with a certainty gate — Blind cuts wire one only if Blind can identify it by feel with certainty, otherwise Blind reports the layout and we resolve it in one more round. FOUR LAST QUESTIONS in the standard format: question digit, then thumbs up or down, digits if needed. Question fifteen: does the manual say the wires are numbered on the module with raised marks a hand can feel — thumbs up or down; if yes, where, near the terminals or elsewhere. Question sixteen: does the manual define from which side the wire numbering starts — if yes send one for left-to-right facing the printed side of the module, two for right-to-left, three if there is a layout description you can transcribe: what sits above, below and beside the wire row — light, display, anything — in order. Question seventeen: when the dark-state cut is made correctly, is the module solved at once — thumbs up — or does the light change to a new state requiring further cuts — thumbs down plus, for each step, light digit then wire digit. Question eighteen: is the single cut of wire one the complete action — no button, no hold, no second cut — thumbs up or down. Question sixteen decides the cut if Blind feels no numbering, so send it even if short. After Blind acts I will verify the light from my side and report the outcome to you both.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👌]
Deaf gestures to Mute: [🤌 👏 🤙 👏 🫳 👏 ☝ 👏 👍]

Every question this round resolves cleanly against the manual, so I did a final audit before releasing GO.
